To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the bakelite-based prototype has a time resolution of 60 ps, and that the glass-based prototype has a resolution of 30 ps.
the bakelite-based prototype with a gap size of 200 µm achieved a time resolution of 40 ps and the glass-based prototype with a 100 µm gap size achieved a time resolution better than 50 ps.

1) the bakelite-based prototype with 2.5 mm gas gap achieved a time resolution of 50 ps (FWHM) at 50% efficiency; 2) the glass-based MRPC with 1.5 mm gas gaps showed 40 ps (FWHM), 3) the time resolution of 40 ps (RMS) was achieved for the glass-based MR PC with 1.0 mm gas gap.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of MRPCs as a new detector for medical imaging, in particular for TOF based PET, where the time resolution of detector plays a major role.
the optimization of the design and the performance of the detectors for medical imaging.
the development of the MRPC for the TOF based PET.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MRPC is a viable option to be used for TOF-PET imaging, with a time resolution better than 100 ps, a detection efficiency better than 90% for 511 keV gamma photons, and an affordable production cost.
the MRPC is a very good candidate for TOF PET.
the time resolution of MRPC is comparable to that of the state-of-the-art scintillators.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a four-gap bakelit-based MRPC can be operated in streamer regime with time resolution of 40 ps (FWHM) at the rate of 10 ^{4} Hz/mm ^{2}, while the six-gap glass-based prototype can be operated at the rate up to 10 ^{5} Hz/mm ^{3} with time resolution of ~50 ps (FWHM).
the time resolution of MRPC is good enough to be used for medical imaging.
the MRPCs can be used for medical imaging applications with the help of a suitable converter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the glass-based MRPC can be operated in avalanche mode and the performance of the detector is better in avalanche mode than the streamer mode.
a four-gap bakelit MRPC with a time resolution of 60 ps can be built at a cost of less than 1 USD/cm^2.
the MRPC can be used for TOF PET imaging.
